question: The management of EU funds requires not only formal checks on their proper use, but also verifying whether the beneficiaries’ activities comply with the conditions and objectives of the funding that has been granted and with the Union policies which the funds are intended to support.

In the context of the Russian Federation’s war of aggression against Ukraine, the EU’s support for Russian civil society organisations and independent media must be subject to strict scrutiny, including those applied to entities operating outside the territory of the Russian Federation. In this connection: 1.

How many times since 2022 has the Commission carried out a review of the activities of Russian civil society organisations and independent media that are beneficiaries of EU funding – including those operating within the Union – to assess their compliance with the objectives of the funding and with EU policies, going beyond the beneficiaries’ own declarations?

Has the Commission identified any instances of beneficiaries’ activities being inconsistent with the objectives of the funding granted or with EU policies as a result of such checks, and if so, how many such instances were identified?
In how many cases did the irregularities identified result in the termination of the contract, the suspension of funding or the initiation of a recovery procedure?
